annotations.title: Opinions citing a federal statute section

description: Lists the opinions whose text cites one U.S. Code section. Federal only: no state statute-citation links exist, and a state citation returns a visible error. An entry means the opinion’s text names the section; it does not say how the court treated it and carries no treatment, validity or "good law" judgment. Zero results is the majority outcome: only 25,093 of 60,444 parseable federal sections (41.5%) have any extracted citing opinion, so an empty list is not evidence that no case cites the statute. Order is most recently filed first and nothing else. The scan covered 10,745,929 opinion records and predates the 2026-09-30 refresh. Every figure is a lower bound with named extraction gaps (no section marker, subsections dropped, only the first section of a list, letter-suffixed sections, ranges). A trailing subsection given is stripped and reported in subsection_dropped. Resolution rates: occurrence-level 0.8870, distinct-pair 0.1697; resolution is not correctness. Precision on a 120-span blind sample: 0.9845 (90% Wilson 0.9526-0.9950); the second extractor alone 0.8667 (0.7785-0.9232); recall unmeasured. parentheticals[] carries any court-written parenthetical verbatim (95.8% of citations have none). section_in_snapshot=false with snapshot_detail marks a section absent from the U.S. Code snapshot; the citation is shown as written, never remapped. Every response, including 400 and 503, carries "note" and "coverage_note". The sources tool returns this tool’s full coverage statement.

cite.description: federal citation as published, e.g. "42 U.S.C. § 1983". A trailing subsection is stripped and reported in subsection_dropped. State citations are refused with a visible error

limit.description: max citing opinions returned, default 25, capped at 50

offset.description: skip this many, for paging further down the date order; capped at 5000

section.description: U.S. Code section number, e.g. "1983" or "1997e". Use with title=

title.description: U.S. Code title, e.g. "42"; used with section= in place of cite=
